lines.0: Namaste Aarav, main Asha, tumhari AI teacher. Aaj cricket score jaise numerals padhenge. Tumhe cricket mein kya pasand hai?
lines.1: Batting pasand hai—accha! End mein cricket score par lautenge. Agar score 3 ho, tum kaunsa numeral chunoge?
lines.2: Bilkul, 3 runs ko numeral 3 likhte hain; screen par 3 objects ke liye bhi 3. Ab 3 ungliyan dikhao.
lines.3: Tumne ek, do, teen gin liye—yeh 3 hain. Ab teen birds udd jaayen, toh kitne birds bachenge?
lines.4: Zero ka matlab hota hai ek bhi nahi. Ab aage kya karenge? Another flies away: ___ is left.
lines.5: Pehle wale step jaisa hi karo: jo birds bache, unhe ek-ek karke gino; phir aage badho. Ab aage kya karenge? Another flies away: ___ is left.
lines.6: Tumne 2 socha. Ab picture mein bache birds ko ek-ek karke count karo, phir unki sankhya ka numeral batao. Ab aage kya karenge? Another flies away: ___ is left.
lines.7: Haan, ek bird bacha—tumne bache hue birds ko ginkar 1 bataya. Main bolti hoon "eight". Ungliyon se 8 dikhao.
lines.8: Theek hai, apna haath dikhao. Five fingers ek haath mein hote hain; ab unke saath aur fingers socho. Main bolti hoon "eight". Ungliyon se 8 dikhao.
lines.9: Tumne 5 aur 3 ko kaise jodkar 8 jaana?
lines.10: Tumne 5 ke baad 6, 7, 8 gin kar 8 banaya. Ab 8 ka numeral batao.
lines.11: Ab isi tarah number ko dekhkar uska naam bolna seekhenge. Tumhare ghar ka number 7 hai. Uske liye kitni taaliyaan bajaoge?
lines.12: Pehle 5 taaliyan gino, phir uske baad ek-ek karke aage gino. Ungliyon se madad le sakte ho. Tumhare ghar ka number 7 hai. Uske liye kitni taaliyaan bajaoge?
lines.13: Haan, 7 taaliyan. Ab 7 ka numeral screen par dikh rahe numbers mein kaunsa hai?
lines.14: Riya kehti hai 6 ko ulta kar do to bhi woh chhah hi rahega. Kya woh sahi hai?

lines.2: Bilkul, 60 se 100 ka jump 40 hai. Ab 30 ke partner se 100 banao: 30 ko kitna chahiye?

lines.4: 46 se 100 ka jump 54 hota hai; ab pehle 46 se 50 tak chhota jump dekho. Khaali jagah bharo: Jump to the next ten: 46 to 50 is ___.
lines.5: Tumne 47, 48, 49, 50 ginkar jump dikhaya. Number line par har agla ank ek jump hota hai. Khaali jagah bharo: Jump to the next ten: 46 to 50 is ___.

lines.12: Tumne ones 5 aur 5 jode, par 65 aur 45 mein tens 6 aur 4 bhi judte hain. 65 ke saath kya milaayein ki 100 ban jaaye?
lines.13: 45 jodne par 110 hota hai; 65 ko pehle 70 karo. 65 se 70 tak kitne ones?

lines.0: Hello Nisha, I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll learn equal shares in fractions. What music do you enjoy?
lines.1: Sorry, I lost my words for a second. Can you say that again?
lines.2: I heard you, Nisha: the Chhota Bheem dholak song, Preeti forgetting words, and your new blue cycle. We’ll return to them later. On screen, one third means three
lines.3: Yes, one third means one equal piece out of three equal pieces. In 15 pencils, what should we do first?
lines.4: Keep going, Nisha—say what each equal group would contain.
lines.5: Yes, Nisha, you made three equal groups of 5 pencils. Fill the gap: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
lines.6: No problem, let's look at this once more, slowly. Fill the gap: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
lines.7: The choices are on screen now. Look at them and think about which number completes the sentence. Fill the gap: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
lines.8: Yes, Nisha: you chose 3, meaning one group out of three equal groups. Two same-sized rectangular school flags each have 4 coloured sections. Flag A has 4 equal
lines.9: You checked whether the parts are equal—that is the key step. Now look at the picture and notice how the sections differ in size. On which flag is one section d
lines.10: You explained that equal parts make one-quarter, while different parts do not. On which flag is one section definitely one-quarter: A or B?
lines.11: You want to stop because you feel tired. You can carry on, take a short break, or stop for today.
lines.12: Of course, Nisha. Take a short break; the lesson waits right here. When you return, we will start gently with the next step.
lines.13: Welcome back, Nisha. How many notes will each group have?
lines.14: You’re right, Nisha—I mentioned notes without showing them. Let’s use 4 equal groups instead: what would one group be called?
